assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of them use a special element called uranium-235 for fission!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an element (uranium-235) but does not describe properties of pure substances, fixed chemical composition, or unique proton numbers. It only names an element used as fuel, which is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What do nuclear power plants use for fuel?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies nuclear fuel (uranium-235) but does not evaluate renewable/non-renewable electricity generation in the Philippines, nor discuss impacts on human activities or the environment. It is only tangentially related to non-renewable energy generation.

copy.en: What do nuclear power plants use for fuel? Most of them use a special element called uranium-235 for fission!
copy.tl: Ano ang ginagamit na gatong ng nuclear power plant? Karamihan sa kanila ay gumagamit ng uranium-235 para sa fission!
copy.bis: Unsay gigamit nga gatong sa nuclear power plant? Kadaghanan kanila mogamit og uranium-235 isip gatong para sa fission!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are 88 official constellations recognized by astronomers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of official constellations recognized by modern astronomers. It does not explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations for direction-finding or season verification, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en:
How many official constellations are hiding in our sky?

There are 88 official constellations recognized by astronomers across the whole sky!
copy.tl:
Ilang opisyal na konstelasyon ang nakatago sa ating langit?

May 88 opisyal na konstelasyon na kinikilala ng mga astronomo sa buong langit!
copy.bis:
Pila ka opisyal nga konstelasyon ang nagtago sa atong langit?

Adunay 88 ka opisyal nga konstelasyon nga giila sa mga astronomo sa tibuok langit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Quantitative observations use numbers and are more useful in science than qualitative ones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses quantitative vs qualitative observations in general science, but does not mention any weather characteristics (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, etc.) or weather data. It shares the broad science vocabulary of observation but provides no direct instructional support for identifying weather characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Quantitative observations use numbers and are more useful in science than qualitative ones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about observation types, not about examining a local weather chart, interpreting weather, or safety precautions. It does not support the specific skill of interpreting weather charts or practicing safety measures, so it is only tangentially related through general science observation concepts.

copy.en: Quantitative observations use numbers and are more useful in science than qualitative ones, which only describe qualities like color or texture.
copy.tl: Ang quantitative observations ay gumagamit ng numero at mas kapaki-pakinabang sa science kaysa qualitative, na naglalarawan lamang ng katangian tulad ng kulay o tekstura.
copy.bis: Ang quantitative observations mogamit ug numero ug mas mapuslanon sa science kay sa qualitative, nga naghulagway lamang sa kinaiya sama sa kolor o tekstura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A nymph looks like a tiny adult insect without wings—with each molt, it grows a little closer to its adult form!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a nymph's appearance and molting, which is a life-cycle stage, but the competency requires using flow charts to compare different stages of specific animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human). The card neither uses a flow chart nor compares stages, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What does a nymph look like?

A nymph looks like a tiny adult insect without wings—with each molt, it grows a little closer to its adult form!
copy.tl:
Ano ang hitsura ng nymph?

Ang nymph ay parang maliit na adult na wala pang pakpak—sa bawat paghuhuklap, unti-unti itong lumalapit sa hugis ng adult!
copy.bis:
Unsay hitsura sa nymph?

Ang nymph murag gamay nga hamtong nga walay pakpak—sa matag paghuklad, hinayhinay kining nagduol sa dagway sa hamtong!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a pigment, which absorbs certain light colors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that pigments absorb certain light colors to produce color, which touches on light behavior, but it does not describe sources of light, how light can be changed, or uses in everyday situations as the competency requires. It is only loosely related to the light topic.

copy.en: Things get color from a pigment, which absorbs certain light colors. Chlorophyll makes leaves green, and melanin gives skin color. Different pigments make different colors!
copy.tl: Ang kulay ay galing sa pigment, na sumisipsip ng ilang kulay ng liwanag. Ang chlorophyll nagpapaberde sa dahon, at melanin nagbibigay kulay sa balat. Iba't ibang pigment, iba't ibang kulay!
copy.bis: Ang kolor gikan sa pigment, nga mosuyop sa pipila ka kolor. Ang chlorophyll naghimo sa dahon nga berde, ug melanin naghatag og kolor sa panit. Lainlain ang pigment, lainlain ang kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object floats when its density is lower than the density of the liquid it is in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains floating in terms of density, not the shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, and gases. It shares the matter topic but does not directly support describing states of matter by shape and volume.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object floats when its density is lower than the density of the liquid it is in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and floating, not physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It is only broadly related to physical properties of matter.

copy.en:
Why do some objects float?

An object floats when its density is lower than the density of the liquid it is in!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang ilang mga bagay?

Lumulutang ang isang bagay kapag mas mababa ang density nito kaysa sa density ng likidong kinalalagyan nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong naglutaw ang ubang mga butang?

Naglutaw ang usa ka butang kung mas ubos ang density niini kaysa sa density sa likido nga gisulodan niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are five: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, and Southern!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card names oceans and notes the Pacific is east of the Philippines, but it does not identify local landforms/bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, or coastlines, nor describe how they influence living and non-living components. It only shares general ocean knowledge.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How many oceans are there on Earth?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists the five oceans but gives no proportion of Earth's surface covered by water versus land, which is the specific skill in G8-E-1. Naming oceans is background vocabulary, not direct support for the proportion concept.

copy.en:
How many oceans are there on Earth?

There are five: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, and Southern! The Pacific is the largest and deepest, located east of the Philippines.
copy.tl:
Ilang karagatan ang mayroon sa mundo?

May lima: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, at Southern! Ang Pacific ang pinakamalaki at pinakamalalim, at nasa silangan ito ng Pilipinas.
copy.bis:
Pila ka kadagatan ang naa sa kalibotan?

Adunay lima: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, ug Southern! Ang Pacific mao ang pinakadako ug pinakalawom, ug naa kini sa sidlakan sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ocean quahog clam named Ming lived to be 507 years old
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the age of a clam; it does not use a flow chart or compare life-cycle stages of any animal. It shares the broad topic of animals but provides no instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ocean quahog clam named Ming lived to be 507 years old
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a living thing and its longevity, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Which animal is the oldest ever found?

An ocean quahog clam named Ming lived to be 507 years old — the oldest individual animal ever found!
copy.tl:
Sino ang pinakamatandang hayop na natuklasan?

Isang ocean quahog clam na tinawag na Ming ang umabot sa 507 taong gulang — ang pinakamatandang indibidwal na hayop na natuklasan!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang pinaka-tigulang nga hayop nga nakit-an?

Usa ka ocean quahog clam nga ginganlan og Ming nakaabot og 507 ka tuig — ang labing tigulang nga indibidwal nga hayop nga nakit-an!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tides have two parts! High tide reaches up the shore, while low tide pulls away from the beach, also called ebb tide.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines high tide and low tide as parts of a tide. It does not mention the Earth, Moon, Sun, or their relative movements, which is the core of the competency. It shares the topic of tides but provides no instructional support for relating celestial movements to tide occurrence.

copy.en: Tides have two parts! High tide reaches up the shore, while low tide pulls away from the beach, also called ebb tide.
copy.tl: May dalawang bahagi ang taog! Umaabot sa dalampasigan ang high tide, habang lumalayo sa baybayin ang low tide o hunas.
copy.bis: Adunay duha ka bahin ang taob! Moabot sa baybayon ang high tide, samtang mopalayo ang low tide o hunas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth has two water bulges at once! One faces the moon, and the other is on the opposite side.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the existence of two tidal bulges and mentions the Moon, but it does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to the occurrence of tides. It lacks the movement/relative-position reasoning required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why do we get two high tides a day?

Earth has two water bulges at once! One faces the moon, and the other is on the opposite side.
copy.tl:
Bakit may dalawang high tide sa isang araw?

May dalawang umbok ng tubig sa Mundo nang sabay! Isa sa harap ng buwan, at isa sa kabilang panig.
copy.bis:
Nganong adunay duha ka high tide sa usa ka adlaw?

Adunay duha ka umbok sa tubig dungan sa Kalibutan! Usa sa atubangan sa bulan, ug usa sa pikas nga kilid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each octopus arm has hundreds of suckers that don't just grip — they can taste whatever they touch.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (arms with suckers) and a sensory function (taste), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. Taste is not movement or food gathering, and the card does not address those roles.

copy.en:
Can an octopus taste with its arms?

Yes! Each octopus arm has hundreds of suckers that don't just grip — they can taste whatever they touch. The arms almost think for themselves!
copy.tl:
Kaya bang tumikim ng pugita gamit ang mga braso?

Oo! Ang bawat braso ng pugita ay may daan-daang suckers na hindi lang humahawak — nakakatikim din ito ng bawat nahihipo. Halos nag-iisip mag-isa ang mga braso!
copy.bis:
Makatilaw ba ang kugita gamit ang iyang bukton?

Oo! Ang matag bukton sa kugita adunay gatusan ka suckers nga dili lang mogunit — motilaw usab kini sa bisan unsang mahikap. Ang mga bukton morag naghunahuna sa ilang kaugalingon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: octopuses have learned mazes, recognized individual people, and even opened screw-top jars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Octopus intelligence is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: octopuses have learned mazes, recognized individual people, and even opened screw-top jars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: Learning mazes is not grow, respond, and reproduce as a set.

copy.en:
How smart are octopuses really?

Very! In experiments, octopuses have learned mazes, recognized individual people, and even opened screw-top jars — surprising intelligence for a mollusk.
copy.tl:
Gaano katalino talaga ang octopus?

Sobra! Sa mga eksperimento, natutunan ng mga octopus ang mga maze, nakilala ang mga tao, at nabuksan pa ang mga garapon — kamangha-manghang talino para sa isang mollusk.
copy.bis:
Unsa ka-abtik gyud ang pugita?

Grabe! Sa mga eksperimento, nakat-onan sa mga pugita ang mga maze, naila ang mga indibidwal nga tawo, ug nabuksan pa ang mga banga — katingalahang katakos alang sa usa ka mollusk.
